heading: Ask your own documents.
summary: We connect AI to your company’s files: PDFs, spreadsheets, wiki pages. Your team asks in plain words and gets an answer with its sources, or an honest “I don’t know”.
lead: We connect AI to your company’s files: PDFs, spreadsheets, wiki pages. Your team asks in plain words and gets an answer with its sources, or an honest “I don’t know”. Try it on a sample logistics company.
privacy: Your files stay in your own database, every answer checks who is asking, and it can all run on your own servers.
demoLabel: Interactive demo: an AI assistant that answers from a logistics company’s own files
stepsLabel: How it works, in five steps

read.text: Your PDFs, spreadsheets and wiki pages, cut into short snippets.

index.text: Snippets about the same topic sit together, so the right ones are found in a blink.

answer.text: Ask in plain words. Every answer shows the file it came from.

guard.text: People only see the files their role allows. No source, no answer.

insights.text: See what your team asks, and what your files don’t cover yet.

scenes.read: Your five files are read and cut into short snippets. Each dot is one snippet, not sorted yet.
scenes.index: Snippets about the same topic pull together. That’s the index: the right ones are found in a blink.
scenes.answer: The question enters the map, hops to the closest snippets, and the answer quotes them as its sources.
scenes.guard: A dispatcher asks about salaries. The search reaches the HR snippets, but the lock stops it: no access, no answer.
scenes.gap: Nothing in the files is close enough, so it says “I don’t know” instead of guessing.
scenes.insights: Every question lands in the insights, and the gap shows what to add to your files next.
